intended_object: A finitely presentable morphism f : X ⟶ Y in a category C, meaning f, viewed as an object of the coslice category X/C (`Under X`), is finitely presentable (ℵ₀-presentable), i.e. Hom_{X/C}(f, -) preserves filtered colimits. Taken from the docstring.
explanation:
The body sends `f` to `ObjectProperty.isFinitelyPresentable.{w} (Under X) (Under.mk f)`, and `ObjectProperty.isFinitelyPresentable` is defined as `IsCardinalPresentable X ℵ₀`. So a morphism f : X ⟶ Y counts as finitely presentable exactly when f is an ℵ₀-presentable object of the coslice category X/C. That is the standard categorical definition (as in Adámek–Rosický and the Stacks Project). In commutative rings, for example, it gives finitely presented algebras.

The definition works for any category C, with the size of the colimits as a universe parameter `w`. This matches how Mathlib states presentability elsewhere, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no morphism-level version of this notion, only the object-level presentability properties it is built from.

One possible generalisation would be κ-presentable morphisms for an arbitrary cardinal κ. That would be a different notion from the one named here, not a broader setting for it, so it does not make this definition too narrow.
